主要内容: San Francisco is set to become the first U.S. city to offer free college tuition to all residents, regardless of financial need. Mayor Ed Lee and Supervisor Jane Kim announced the plan, which would provide nearly $5.4 million annually to the City College of San Francisco. The initiative, expected to take effect in the fall, would benefit over 28,000 students and allow any resident who has lived in the city for at least a year to qualify. Full-time low-income students who already receive fee waivers would receive an additional $250 per semester. The city also plans to provide one-time funding of $500,000 to help implement the changes. This move marks a significant step in the push for free college education, with similar proposals in New York and support from former President Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton.
